themes: Bed boom in KIMS's home city
At least 4-5 hospitals opened in Hyderabad in the year to May-2026 (CEO); KIMS added Kompally and the 787-bed Kondapur itself. Hyderabad is 'the most competitive' of its markets for doctors.

New hospitals waited months for insurer and PSU panels in FY26 as the General Insurance Council's common-empanelment plan caused confusion; Thane, Nashik and Bengaluru were ~50% empanelled by Aug-2026, the rest expected by mid-September.
Insurance rose from 30% (FY26) to 32% (Q1FY27) of KIMS's revenue, corporate 12%; cash is still 52%, unusually high for a listed chain, which reflects tier-2 Andhra and Telangana.
Aarogyasri (the state scheme the founder helped design in 2007) is now only 4-5% of revenue; government receivables were slow in FY26 (CFO).
Sector ARPOB +6-8% a year (ICRA); KIMS guides only 4-5%, with oncology and transplants being added in Andhra and at Kondapur.
Full-time doctor models are easy to staff in the South but slow in Maharashtra, where doctors first join part-time (Nagpur took 18-24 months to stabilise).
Operators now run hospitals for a fee with options to buy: KIMS has five fee-based O&M hospitals (Sangli, Guntur x2, Kompally, Arete, Kakinada) at ~9% of revenue.
industry.src: ICRA (Jul-2026); KIMS Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls and presentations; GAM Research

moat: Density in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
Advantage

~5,000 capacity beds in the two states; Telangana earned a 30.4% EBITDA margin in FY26 and 77% of group EBITDA in Q1FY27; the deck claims No. 1 positions in cardiac, neuro, nephrology and urology treatment in Andhra Pradesh.
Referral networks and doctor loyalty in the home market; hard to replicate quickly.
Affordable tertiary care at low cost
Advantage
Group ARPOB ₹47,200 (Q1FY27), well below metro chains, yet Telangana margins of ~30% and Andhra 22-25% at ARPOB of only ~₹25,000.
A cost model that works in tier-2 towns; the price point limits margins in costlier metros.
Doctor-partnership model
Moderate
Doctors own equity in ten hospital companies; aligns incentives and helps recruit, but leaks 7-8% of profit to minorities and needs buy-outs (₹150 cr for Sunshine in FY26).
Works in the South; in Maharashtra doctors are slow to go full-time.
Clinical depth
Moderate
Heart, lung, liver and kidney transplants, large ECMO programme, robotics; oncology being added in Andhra and at Kondapur.
Supports ARPOB growth; peers offer the same in metros.
Brand outside the home states
Weak
Bengaluru, Thane, Nashik and Kerala are 1-2 years old; insurer empanelment took most of FY26; Bengaluru lost ₹91 cr of EBITDA in FY26.
The moat is regional; new markets have to be won against Manipal, Apollo, Aster and others.
Pricing power
Moderate
ARPP +11% in FY26 and +7% in Q1FY27 (mostly mix); management guides ARPOB +4-5% a year.
Price is not the lever; occupancy and mix are.
Payer mix
Parity
Cash 52%, insurance 32%, corporate 12%, government schemes 4% (Q1FY27); FY26 showed weak bargaining power with insurers for new hospitals.
High cash share helps margins but caps volumes in insured metro patients.
Balance sheet
Weak
Net debt ₹4,386 cr at Mar-26 including leases and minorities (5.4x FY26 EBITDA), cut to ~₹2,300 cr pro forma by ₹2,076 cr of new equity; promoters pledged 6.67% of the company in Sep-2026.
Expansion has relied on debt and dilution; free cash flow only turns solidly positive in FY28-29E.
critiques: Growth has been bought with capital: ~₹3,100 cr of capex in FY24-26, net debt to ~5x EBITDA, then a ₹1,500 cr QIP and ₹600 cr of promoter warrants (7% dilution)

gaps: Hospital-level P&L is disclosed only for a few new units (chart labels in the Q1FY27 deck); mature hospitals (Secunderabad, Kondapur, Sunshine) are described only qualitatively (34-39% margins). EBITDA per bed and capex per bed by unit are not disclosed.
Unit EBITDA mapping for Nashik and Thane is our reading of chart labels and conflicts with the Q4FY26 call figures (see conflicts).
Who owns the other 59.5% of Kondapur Healthcare Ltd (the associate that owns the new Kondapur building) and the lease terms KIMS pays it were not found in sources dated before 30-Sep-2026.
Minority interests' share of profit by subsidiary could not be read reliably from the AR FY26 entity table (note 2.37 is rotated); we use group totals and management's 10-15% long-term guide.
Start-up losses for FY23-24 are not disclosed (no greenfield opened in FY24); the start-up-adjusted multiple adds back only FY25 (₹18.3 cr), FY26 (₹128 cr) and our FY27-29E estimates.
Rent (Ind AS 116 impact) for FY27-29E and lease liabilities beyond Mar-26 are our estimates; used only to translate pre-Ind AS figures.

conflicts: Unit losses Q4FY26: the CEO said Thane ~₹5 cr and Nashik ~₹1 cr; the Q1FY27 deck's chart labels read ~₹9 cr and ~₹1.5 cr. Bengaluru figures agree (Mahadevapura ₹14-15 cr, Electronic City ₹25 cr).
FY25 occupancy is shown as 50.0%, 50.1%, 52.7% and 53.0% in different decks because operational beds were redefined (4,492 / 4,267 / 4,239). We use the latest deck.
FII holding at Jun-2026: 14.75% (BSE pattern via Screener) vs 17.4% (company deck, which counts some foreign holders differently). We use Screener for the time series and the deck for named holders.
Axis Securities' EPS uses 40.0 cr shares and PL's 42.0 cr; our per-share figures use 42.77 cr (fully diluted for the warrants).

Q4FY26 call: management called the post-QIP leverage target 'net debt to EBITDA of 1 is to 2' (i.e. ~2x); Q1FY27 call: 'debt equity in the range of 2.5:1' (as transcribed). We read the target as ~2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA.
